extracted.intended_audience: prospective FRO founders, funders, entrepreneurial scientists, and partners interested in launching grant-funded scientific infrastructure organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and expectations for creating, structuring, funding, and operating a Convergent FRO (Foundry / focused research organization) — including funding levels, time horizon, team composition, goals, deliverables, and the support Convergent provides before and after launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial grant size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FROs are launched with substantial up-front funding in this range to enable focused, multi-year work rather than small pilot budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-bound duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergent FROs work for 3-7 years on high-impact technical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FROs are explicitly time-limited efforts (not indefinite orgs); the 3–7 year window sets expectations for planning, milestones, and exit outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time teams and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs are led by full-time executives and bring together teams of 10-30+ engineers, scientists, and operators working together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operates as a staffed, mission-driven organization (not a side project) with dedicated leadership and personnel to ensure focused, rapid progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission to build public tools / public goods
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs have a mission to build public tools that unlock new progress across entire fields. They create public goods that are technically ambitious and engineering-heavy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs should be public-facing infrastructure (tools, datasets, platforms) intended to seed ecosystems and enable scaled change in their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on infrastructure-heavy, cross-cutting problems
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs were created because some problems in science are too complex, too cross-cutting, or too infrastructure-heavy for universities, startups, or traditional labs to solve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select problems where traditional actors are unlikely to deliver the required large-scale infrastructure or coordination; FROs target bottlenecks across domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technically ambitious, engineering-heavy research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research produced by FROs often looks like tools, datasets, and scientific infrastructure and is engineering-heavy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect deliverables to emphasize engineering, productization, and scalable technical systems rather than narrow academic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release outputs as products
rubrics_metrics.description: Our FROs release these goods as products that can seed an ecosystem of users and drive a scaled revolution in their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize product-quality releases that enable adoption and ecosystem growth rather than solely publishing academic artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified, quantifiable technical milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: They pursue pre-specified, quantifiable technical milestones, with milestones and external reviews marking their progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear, measurable milestones in advance and use external review checkpoints to assess progress and de-risk continuation or transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational form: nonprofit run like a startup
rubrics_metrics.description: Each FRO is a nonprofit that runs like a startup, not a side project, so its culture feels tight-knit, fast-moving, & mission-driven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt startup operational norms (speed, tight teams, product focus) within a nonprofit legal/financial structure suited for public-good outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founders profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Founded by entrepreneurial scientists who want to unblock progress in their fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders are expected to be technically credible scientists with entrepreneurial orientation and commitment to building and shipping infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergent pre-launch support (programmatic incubation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a FRO can launch, Convergent provides programmatic incubation, supporting scoping, technical roadmapping, operational planning, budgeting, and fundraising efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective FROs receive hands-on help to define scope, create technical roadmaps, build operational plans, produce budgets, and prepare fundraising strategies prior to formal launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent nonprofit post-launch support
rubrics_metrics.description: After launch, as a parent non-profit, Convergent provides our subsidiary FROs with governance and critical operations support so they can efficiently deliver the public goods they are founded to produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing governance, administrative, and operational back-office support is expected from Convergent to let FRO teams focus on technical delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable outcomes for successful FROs
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs that reach their goals of producing a critical piece of scientific infrastructure have a range of possible outcomes, from selling products and services as a non-profit, to perpetual endowment as a foundation, to commercialization by licensing to a for-profit company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define potential exit/transition paths in advance (continued nonprofit operations, endowment, or commercialization/licensing) aligned with the public-good mission and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on measurable, field-unblocking impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Focused: Each FRO is a time-bound, technically ambitious effort designed to unblock whole domains of technical progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core evaluative criterion is whether the FRO's work materially unblocks progress across a domain — impact should be scoped and measured against that goal.
